messages:
Kai: Ran the nightly perf sweep with FP8 KV-cache enabled on Qwen-70B (mixed seqs up to 2048). Seeing 99.9 tail latency spike ~2.1x vs BF16 baseline :eyes:
Alex: timeline? which kernel path got chosen for those invocations?
Kai: profiler shows fallback to the new `kv_dequant_fp8` path intermittently; most of the time kernel=matmul_auto_select_v3 but dequant step dominates.
Siobhan: pasted trimmed profiler excerpt:```
# sample 1
kernel matmul_auto_select_v3 time=9.7ms
kv_load time=1.8ms
kv_dequant_fp8 time=7.4ms  # huge
memcpy time=0.6ms
```
Maria: confirming — the `dequantize_kv_fp8` op is single-threaded on CPU in our current implementation when prefix split occurs. That aligns with the spike when long prefixes + dynamic batching collapse many requests together.
Alex: interesting — so it's not pure GPU matmul being slow, it's the CPU dequant + memcpy causing the tail. Any correlation with RoPE scaling changes?
Siobhan: yes — we rolled a small RoPE scaling tweak for Qwen last week (head_dim normalization change). It changes effective kv layout for some head/kv dimensions and triggers a slower code path in the quantized loader.
Devex: steps to reproduce locally?
Kai: quick repro script:```bash
python tools/run_perf.py --model qwen-70b --seq-len 2048 --prefix 1024 --enable-kv-quant=fp8 --batching=dynamic
```
Alex: tried forcing fallback to FP16 kernels (`KERNEL_FORCE=fp16`) — tail collapses to baseline but memory increases ~8-12% and throughput drops a bit.
Maria: tradeoff noted. Also saw that when we lower dynamic batching threshold from 16->8 the dequant contention reduces significantly for long-prefix traffic.
Siobhan: hypothesis: FP8 quant path is beneficial for cold-start and mem footprint, but when prefix churn + batching produces many small KV merges we pay heavy CPU dequant cost per merged request.
Devex: proposal: three experiments (A/B):
  1) Disable FP8 for Qwen canary (quick rollback path)
  2) Keep FP8 but route dequant onto GPU (prototype kernel exists)
  3) Keep FP8 but tighten batching heuristic for long-prefix requests (threshold=8, max_concat=3)
Alex: + add a variant that forces BF16 dequant (dequant->bf16->gpu) to measure latency vs mem tradeoff.
Kai: scheduled runs: Ops-bot queued experiments on `dedicated-gpu-pool-7` starting 2025-10-21T03:00Z.
Ops-bot: Experiments created: exp-qa-1765123456-A,B,C — logs to s3://redwood-perf/exp-qa-1765123456/
Maria: I'll own B and BF16 variant, Siobhan will run A and the batching tweak.
Siobhan: side note — Mixtral had a similar regression last quarter but it was masked by different RoPE mapping; adding small unit test in runtime that validates head_dim->kv_stride mapping prevents silent kernel-path flips.
Kai: added task to PR: runtime/tests/test_kv_layout_rope_mapping.py — will add a micro-benchmark too.
Alex: add instrumentation: `--kv-trace=ops,dequant,merge --profile=gpu,cpu` and capture `kv-samples/1765123456.log` to speed triage.
Devex: also surface a dashboard panel for kv-dequant latency (p50/p95/p99.9) and prefix-length buckets.
Kai: agreed. After runs land I'll post the perf dashboard link and suggested rollout plan (canary gating rules: 99.9 <= baseline*1.1).
Maria: one last note — if GPU dequant kernel is stable it might be the long-term win: preserves mem benefits of FP8 while avoiding CPU memcpy stalls. But we need to verify device-to-host sync overhead doesn't negate gains.
Kai: ok let's sync tomorrow 10:30 PT with data from the first two experiments. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
